supporting_observations.claim: The observed periodic HTTPS activity was routed through the organization's proxy to update.medledger.com, with successful CONNECT tunnels at approximately five-minute intervals from 13:40:50 through 14:10:29 UTC.

The network events are attributed to C:\Program Files\MediLedger\medledgerupd.exe, including repeated process-attributed connections to the proxy; the asset/service inventory identifies this updater and update.medledger.com as approved and says it checks about every five minutes.

The updater was launched by tom.weber's PowerShell process, which is an unusual context worth noting, but the available records do not show the PowerShell command line or establish that the updater or its network activity was malicious.

known_telemetry_limitations: The proxy records show CONNECT tunnels and byte counts, not the encrypted HTTPS request or response contents; for example, T096-00074 records a tunnel to update.medledger.com.

The supplied process and network records do not include a hash or signature validation for medledgerupd.exe; T096-00070 identifies its path and process context but does not establish binary integrity.
claims_not_established: The contents of the encrypted HTTPS exchanges and whether the updater downloaded or applied an update.
Whether the updater binary was authentic and unmodified.
What command or script in PowerShell launched the updater.
unrelated_findings: The proxy recorded a connection to docs.google.com, an unapproved cloud/file-sharing service in the supplied inventory; this is separate from the alerted MediLedger activity. (T096-00176, T096-00177, T096-00178, T096-00179)

Cisco AnyConnect and Palo Alto GlobalProtect clients were launched on WS-TWEBER-01 despite the inventory stating there is no VPN; these records show process launches, not successful VPN connections. Review separately. (T096-00143, T096-00144, T096-00145, T096-00274, T096-00275, T096-00276)
